title: E-Commerce Real-Time Full-Text Search & Faceted Filtering
businessContext: An e-commerce retailer with 25,000,000 product SKUs needs sub-50ms search with autocomplete, typo tolerance, synonyms, faceted aggregations (brand, category, price ranges, rating), and real-time inventory filtering.
problemStatement: Architect an enterprise search engine cluster (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch). Describe the document indexing pipeline from PostgreSQL via CDC, the inverted index and BKD tree structure, shard distribution, query DSL construction for boolean query scoring with BM25, and zero-downtime index re-indexing via index aliases.
constraints: Search query P99 latency: < 50ms across 25M products.
Freshness: New products or price changes searchable within 3 seconds of DB commit.
Support typo tolerance (Levenshtein edit distance 1-2) without killing performance.

functional: Full-text query search with BM25 relevance scoring.
Faceted navigation (aggregations on price, color, brand).
assumptions: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch used as search secondary index.

candidateTasks: Design the inverted index document mapping with analyzers (stemming, lowercase, edge_ngram for autocomplete).
Explain BM25 relevance scoring algorithm (term frequency, inverse document frequency, document length normalization).
Design the zero-downtime re-indexing strategy using Index Aliases (`products_v1` -> `products_v2` with `_aliases` switch).
Design faceted aggregations using doc_values for low memory footprint.
hints: Inverted indexes map terms to document IDs for text search; BKD trees index numeric values (prices, ratings) for range filters.
Never point application directly to an index name (`products`); point to an alias (`products_active`) so you can swap versions atomically.
alternativeApproaches: PostgreSQL `pgvector` + `pg_trgm` if catalog is smaller than 200k items.
Algolia / Meilisearch for managed developer-friendly search.
commonMistakes: Running wildcards `*term*` in production: leading wildcards bypass inverted indexes and force a full cluster scan.
Putting filters in the `must` clause instead of `filter` clause, calculating unnecessary relevance scores for boolean attributes and preventing cache utilization.
